1.  The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Vivek Kumar, aged about 24 years, suffered grievous injury and amputation of his right lower limb.

An application u/s 166(1)
Motor Vehicle Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/applicant seeking compensation.
A separate claim petition was filed with respect to the same accident by another victim Govid Babu which is registered as MACT No. 412/25.

Brief facts of the case are that on 31.01.2022 at about 08:00 a.m., victim petitioner along with one Govind Babu, was going towards Kanpur from District Etawa on a motorcycle bearing no.UP-75AM-3179.
The motorcycle was being driven by the petitioner.

When they reached in front of Kanchan Hotel Sikandra, a speeding truck coming from Orreya bearing no.HR-69B-6768 (hereinafter referred as to the offending vehicle) at a high speed, driven in a rash and negligent manner hit the motorcycle.
Due to the collision petitioner and Govind Babu fell on the road and sustained injuries.
They were removed to the Zila Chikitsalaya Akbarpur where right leg of the victim Vivek had to be amputed to treat him while Govind was treated for grievous injuries.

sentences.text: It is argued on behalf of the claimants that the accident was caused by respondent no.1 by driving the offending motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner.
It is argued that since respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle, which is owned by him and insured with respondent no. 2, both the respondents are liable to compensate the petitioner.

On the other hand, it is the argument of respondent no. 2 that the insurance company with which such offending vehicle was insured cannot be fastened with liability to compensate the petitioners as neither negligence of respondent no.1 is proved nor the occurrence of the accident.
9.

On the basis of pleadings of the parties, evidence adduced and arguments addressed, issue wise findings are as under:
Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 31.01.2022 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR69B-6768 being driven and owned by R1 and insured with R2? OPP 10.

Before proceeding to decide the above issue, it is apposite to note that as a settled principle of law, proceedings under The Motor Vehicle Act are not considered akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not applicable.

Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs.
Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana,
2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and MACT No.1096/24 Vivek Kumar v. Surender Kumar & anr.

11. In the instant case, respondents have taken a defence as to the involvement of the offending vehicle in the alleged accident.

In order to prove, the involvement of the offending vehicle petitioner Vivek Kumar vs Surender Kumar on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95040856/
4 examined himself as PW-1 wherein he testified that the accident took place when the motorcycle which was being driven by victim Vivek Kumar was hit from behind by the offending truck.
Upon being cross-examined on behalf of respondent/driver-cum-owner, PW-1 admitted that he was looking in front at the time of accident but saw the alleged offending vehicle coming from behind.
He further testified that he was conscious after the accident.
Despite this fact, the registration number of the offending vehicle was never disclosed by the victim at the first instance even to the doctor who examined him.
None of the medical documents, beginning from the first hospital where the victim was taken till the last one, mentions the registration number of the offending vehicle.

Though furnishing of details of the alleged vehicle may not be mandatory to be disclosed to the treating doctor, it is crucial that such details must have been informed to the police at least, soon after the accident.
In the present case, the FIR has been registered after a delay of almost three months from the accident.

Despite the fact that the victim was in a conscious state and also accompanied by his family members during his treatment, the registration number of the alleged offending vehicle was never disclosed.

Such non-disclosure of the information and details of the offending vehicle coupled with the fact that even the mechanical inspection report of the involved vehicle has not been MACT No.1096/24 Vivek Kumar v. Surender Kumar & anr. P.No. 7 Of 10 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.05.07 16:01:53 +0530 placed, further renders the involvement of such vehicle doubtful.

entities.text: MACT No.1096/24 Vivek Kumar v. Surender Kumar & anr. P.No. 7 Of 10 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This is particularly so as the driver of the alleged offending vehicle has also led evidence testifying that his vehicle was never involved in any accident as alleged by the petitioner.

Respondent no.1, testifying as RW-1 has also stated that it is only pursuant to a call received on 28.03.2022 from mobile no. 7571830066 by someone introducing himself as Sanjesh Kumar, investigating officer from police station Sikandra that the respondent was informed about involvement of his vehicle in the accident.
He has further deposed that even his TIP was never conducted by the concerned police and thus, there was nothing to establish the identity of the vehicle involved in the alleged accident.
During cross examination RW1 further denied that the offending truck was ever seized by the police or released on superdari.
Petitioner has filed no evidence on record to show that the offending truck was seized by the police or if seized, the date of the same.
It is pertinent to note that in the alleged accident it was not only the petitioner /victim Vivek who suffered injuries but also one Govind Babu who allegedly got injured.
In fact, a referral slip issued by Sanyukt Zila Chikitsalaya qua the treatment of victim Govind also does not mention the details of the vehicle.

Such medical slip does not reveal any medical condition of Govind Babu preventing him from disclosing the details of the offending vehicle for 3 months, despite the fact that he was discharged from such hospital on the same day.

Also there is no continuity in the treatment record relied upon by victim Govind Babu which leads to an inference that the details of the actual offending vehicle may not have been known or noted by either of MACT No.1096/24 Vivek Kumar v.
Surender Kumar & anr. P.No. 8 Of 10 ss CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.05.07 16:01:57 +0530 the victims.

sentences.text: Respondents have also examined the owner of the offending vehicle as R1W2 who has testified that he had accompanied driver of the offending vehicle to the police station on 04.04.2022.

Vivek Kumar vs Surender Kumar on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95040856/
5

It is observed that despite denial by driver as well as the owner of the offending vehicle qua the involvement of the alleged vehicle, no document has been produced or evidence has been led to show the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.

The delay of 3 months in lodging of the FIR in such circumstances, where the driver and owner of the offending vehicle deny the involvement and led evidence, while no evidence is brought forth by the petitioner to establish that the involvement of a particular vehicle was informed by him to the police at the initial stage,
becomes detrimental to the case of the petitioner and raises serious doubt qua involvement of the offending vehicle.

12. In these circumstances, though there is no evidence to the contrary to disbelieve the occurrence of the accident, there is serious and considerable doubt in believing that such an accident was caused by the offending vehicle.
It is possible that the offending vehicle may not have been identified and may have remained untrace and only to secure compensation, details of the offending vehicle may have been planted later on.
As such, instead of dismissing the case, the present petition is being treated as a case of offending vehicle remaining untraced.
Issue no.2 MACT No.1096/24 Vivek Kumar v. Surender Kumar & anr. P.No. 9 Of 10 ss Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA

OPP. 
13.
For the reason discussed in issue no.1, claimants are held not entitled to any compensation from the respondents.
Issue no.2 is accordingly decided against the petitioners/claimants.
However, since only the involvement of the offending vehicle is not proved but probability of occurrence of the accident is proved, the case may be treated as a case where the offender is not traced.

As per Section 396(4) of (BNSS) Baratiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita:
"Where the offender is not traced or identified, but the victim is identified, and where no trial takes place, the victim or his dependents may make an application to the State or the District Legal Services Authority for award of compensation".

As such, petitioners are at liberty to approach concerned State Legal Services Authority for relief, if permissible.
14.
Hence, in view of the observation made above, present petition stands disposed of.
15. File be consigned to the record room.
